props.title: Who else uses this, in one glance
props.subtitle: Real customer logos, with permission. No customers yet? Show partners, press or certifications — never invent them.

items.description: A sentence naming the problem before and the measured result after. Numbers make it credible.
A quote that answers the same doubt your FAQ answers: time to value, price or trust.
Ask three customers for one sentence each: what was hard before, what changed, and a number. Use their real name, role and photo with permission.

props.title: The six sections of a lead generation page
props.subtitle: Presence matters more than order: visitors scan, then read. Each block answers a question they have not asked yet.

items.title: A promise in the headline
items.description: Say what the visitor gets, in their words. “Get the checklist” beats “Download our PDF”.

items.title: The offer, made concrete
items.description: Describe the magnet as a thing with a shape: pages, minutes, steps. Show it if you can.

items.title: Proof someone else trusted you
items.description: One real sentence from a customer outperforms three generic ones. Never invent them.

items.title: The form, short and visible
items.description: Ask only for what the follow-up needs. Make the button describe the outcome.

items.title: Objections answered
items.description: An FAQ handles price, privacy, time and fit without a sales call — and feeds structured data.

items.title: The same ask, repeated
items.description: Visitors who reached the end are the most convinced. Give them the same action, not a new one.

props.title: Asked before filling in a form

items.title: What is a lead generation landing page?
items.description: A single page with one goal: exchange something valuable — a guide, a demo, a quote, a trial — for a visitor’s contact details. Unlike a homepage it has no competing navigation and repeats one call to action.

items.title: How many fields should the form have?
items.description: As few as your follow-up needs. Name and email are enough for a download; add company or budget only when sales will actually use them. Every extra required field lowers completion.

items.title: Above the fold or at the end?
items.description: Both, and the same form. In the first screen for visitors who arrive convinced, repeated after the proof for those who need the full story. Two placements, one offer.

items.title: What is a good conversion rate?
items.description: It depends on the source. Cold paid traffic often converts in the low single digits; warm email or retargeting can reach 10–20%. Compare against your own baseline and change one thing at a time.

items.title: Does this satisfy privacy consent?
items.description: The form ships with a consent checkbox linked to the privacy policy. Keep the label explicit about what you send and how often, and store the consent alongside the lead.
